recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed; if PA still wants a separately maintained earlier-version standard extension, that should be handled as an Extension Pack or work-group follow-up rather than as a correction to the current core Practitioner resource.
issue_request: FHIR-17634 asked PA to add a Practitioner deceased indicator modeled on Patient.deceased[x], with boolean and dateTime choices, to help detect prescription validity and fraud after prescriber death. The Published/Persuasive resolution described adding the property as a standard extension usable in earlier FHIR versions.
initial_application: Commit 353b3b965d8b2975d5ceaf02cee00c154daf1e38 explicitly cited FHIR-17634 and FHIR-26590 and added Practitioner.deceased[x] plus Practitioner death-date and deceased search parameters to source/practitioner. The historical application landed as a core Practitioner element rather than as a standalone standard extension.
additional_context: FHIR-26590 later/pairwise requested the core Practitioner.deceased[x] element and search parameter directly, was Published/Persuasive for R5, and is already represented on the combined branch by 8fb6be07d335d4ca063d3cfdc7bbcaf502737d54. FHIR-37897 later added the modifier flag and reason now present in source and is already represented by da24b911e6d9e7df6e38823d6a9b7e2f5924c941. FHIR-37902 resolved no-change on adding an unknown/code data type, supporting the current boolean/dateTime shape. Practitioner is active in source/fhir.ini, and no current Practitioner-deceased standard extension was found in the core extension/profile sources or the Extension Pack checkout.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current active Practitioner StructureDefinition already contains Practitioner.deceased[x] as 0..1 boolean/dateTime with isModifier=true and a historical-use modifier reason, and the Practitioner search parameter bundle contains the deceased and death-date search parameters. Given FHIR-26590's later final core-element decision, replacing or duplicating the current element with a standard extension would make the current build less consistent.
